---
title: "Agentic coding"
---

Agentic coding tools wrote this software. This page states what the tools wrote, what the
author decided, and which checks the result must pass.

## What the tools wrote

Agentic coding tools wrote the implementation: the solver, the controls, the derivatives,
the tests, the examples and this documentation. The author directed the work and reviewed
it. The physics and the method are not new. They come from CODE-A and from the papers on
[the home page](index.qmd).

## What the author decided

The author gave 26 numbered rulings. They set the scope: what is ported and what is not.
They set the physics: self-consistent gravity, the compressibility and gravity flags, free
slip or no slip, and density jumps as phase changes. They also set the conventions (those
of lovejx), the default motion of the movable boundaries, how the tests run, and the form
of this documentation and its deployment. The tools proposed the other design defaults and every tolerance. One
ruling accepts the defaults of the open questions of the chunk plans that it names. The
questions that no ruling decides keep the default of the package. [The open
points](open-points.qmd) list those that change what a user sees.

## How the tolerances were set

Each tolerance states its cause next to its value in the test code. When a planned
tolerance did not hold, the tools loosened it only with an entry in the tolerance log of
the author's working notes. The entry holds the old value, the new value, the measured
value and the cause. For example, the bound of the derivative on the stiff-lid case
against the high-precision solver went from 1e-12 to 1e-10. The package measured 9.7e-12
in forward mode and 1.6e-11 in reverse mode. The cause is the rounding on the thin stiff lid.

## What checks the result

- Separate review agents checked each plan and each implementation.
- Two references are not the work of a tool: the Fortran golden output of CODE-A (under
  CODE-A's own switches), and the analytical solutions of Kramer, Davies and Wilson (2021)
  through `assess`.
- The mpmath solver is a second solver, which the tools wrote from the same equations
  with another algorithm and another arithmetic.
- The Taylor policy has negative controls, and a measurement that the rounding hides is
  not a pass.
- One test run holds every check.

[The validation page](validation.qmd) gives the detail, and [the open
points](open-points.qmd) state what is not checked yet.
